english.title: Possess ammunition for a firearm when prohibited for life - Firearms Act 1968
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person who had been sentenced to

(A)_[imprisonment]_
(B)_[preventive detention]_
(C)_[corrective training]_
(D)_[youth custody]_
(E)_[detention in a Young Offender Institution]_

for a term of **(..SPECIFY THE NUMBER OF YEARS - WHICH MUST BE AT LEAST THREE YEARS FOR THIS SUBSECTION TO APPLY..) had in your possession ammunition for a firearm
english.legislation: Contrary to section 21(1) and (4) of and Schedule 6 to the Firearms Act 1968.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being a person who had been sentenced to imprisonment/preventive detention/corrective training or
youth custody/detention in a young offender Institution
for a term of three years or more possessed ammunition for a firearm

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The custodial sentences to which this section applies are preventative detention or imprisonment, corrective training, youth custody and detention in a Young Offenders Institution for three years or more, and custody for life.
(ii) It is the period of the sentence that is important not the actual time served by the offender.
(iii) See also associated offence wordings as follows: H1799, H2211, H2219 and H2225.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Five years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
